also: put the fear of God into

evidence: Cic. Fam. 2.16.4: nec mē ista terrent
terms.comment: “Scared” is territus; being afraid is timēre (see be afraid).

terms.register: Lewis & Short: poetic and very rare

terms.comment: Literally “you make me shudder”; horreō, to bristle, shudder.

phrases.latin: Nec mē ista terrent quae mihi ā tē ad timōrem fīdissimē atque amantissimē prōpōnuntur.
phrases.english: Nor am I frightened by the things you so faithfully and lovingly set before me to make me afraid.

phrases.latin: pater deōrum rīsit atque illīs dedit parvum tigillum, missum quod subitō vadī mōtū sonōque terruit pavidum genus
phrases.english: the father of the gods laughed and gave them a little log, which, thrown in, frightened the timid race with the sudden stir and splash of the water
